Is it delivering?

About this view

Every snapshot is one gauge card (Jason, 2026-11-22): its dial or bar against its target's bands, the band's word under the needle, the reading with its time, and its trend. Tap a card for its snapshot; Workflows ▸ and Services ▸ drill down to the root, computed from the association map (step3/association-map.md). This supersedes step 1's "skip big gauges" (Q21; SM 172–189).

Development

configurations drafted, awaiting Jason's sign-off

Each gauge starts at 0 in Planning and is configured to say what 100 means (Jason, 2026-11-22). The word under the needle is its stage: Planning → Phased Development → Audit & Review → Implementation → Monitoring, the stage of the work (Jason, 2026-11-22). One needle: criteria met over criteria configured; the word is a label, never a second needle.

The criteria come from the page audit (decisions/0145). Checked: the audit's code, rendered and path checks pass at 1280 and 390. Reviewed: the page review has no open finding, and Jason has signed off (his UI, UX and Functional approval on a release, or his ruling on the page's proposal). Proved: the path or function check on live data. Past work without his sign-off on record shows "audited, awaiting sign-off", never "reviewed". Complete needs a path or function check; a page that only renders isn't complete.

One item not yet built keeps the whole gauge in Phased Development; the needle still shows progress.

A runtime gauge under the lifecycle: Pages load fast, stage by stage approved by Jason, 2026-11-22; only Planning is today, the rest are illustrations

Setup (the probe built, its target set by Jason, its check passing on its clock, its alarm wired to the board) is the needle through Planning to Implementation. At Monitoring the needle switches to the live reading against its target, and setup shows only in Configure. One needle at a time.

  • CRAWLER_API_TOKEN: .env and Railway (the crawler's pass into our endpoints)
  • VIDEO_WORKER_TOKEN: .env and Railway (the video worker's pass into our endpoints)
  • HEALTH_TOKEN: .env and a GitHub secret (they must match) (the daily health report)

What the system is doingThe outside heartbeat (GitHub Actions) checks every 15–30 minutes (next 2:30 AM MST) and writes the incident as an unnumbered record in the repo. It emails <the address set as ALARM_TO> (a GitHub secret, never hard-coded; unset, the heartbeat's run fails visibly on GitHub), only, through the site's Amazon email (SES); no push while the host is gone. When the site is back it takes the record in, numbers it, and shows it in Pulse as “Raised while the site was down, by the outside heartbeat”.

Certificates (TLS)
one per hostname, asked for through Fly's API
The job domains_tick (every 15 minutes) checks each waiting domain's DNS, then its certificate: Added → DNS pointed → Certificate coming → Live; Failed; Removed. Live ones are checked once a day; one whose DNS has moved away for 3 days goes to Failed and its storefront back to trvgo.us. Disconnect removes its certificates.

Its rules: the AI monthly cap (ai_month_usd, $40.00 in the live reading) stops every feature for the month; Guides on demand may spend up to half the day's allowance (the cap ÷ the days in the month; guide_ondemand_share, 50 by default), and a build that would pass it queues for tomorrow, most-searched first; a build never stops part way (0147 §5). Each feature also has its own runs a day and budget (AI use). Every call's cost is counted, a failed call after a paid answer included (0160 §5, D16). Defaults from the code; the live settings per feature: not read yet.

Where its keys live:
  • SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD: .env (Bluehost's mail server: system email, first)
  • SMTP_FROM_EMAIL, SMTP_FROM_NAME, SMTP_REPLY_TO: .env (who system email is from)
  • <SENDER>_SMTP_USERNAME, <SENDER>_SMTP_PASSWORD: .env (a sender's own mailbox, where it has one)
  • SES_MODE, SES_REGION (else AWS_REGION): .env (Amazon SES: off, mock or live)
  • AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (or SES_PERSONAL_KEY_ID, SES_PERSONAL_SECRET): .env (SES's personal account: notices, digests, the backup for system email)
  • SES_BULK_KEY_ID, SES_BULK_SECRET: .env (SES's bulk account, when bulk mail is built)
  • SES_MONTHLY_CAP_USD, SES_USD_PER_1000, EMAIL_LINK_KEY: .env (SES's cap and price; unsubscribe links)
  • VAPID_PRIVATE_PEM_B64, VAPID_PUBLIC_B64U: .env (write-only) (web push: our own keys)
  • COMMS_SEAL_KEY: .env (write-only) (seals the mailboxes' passwords)
  • Mailboxes' passwords and Microsoft's tokens: the database, sealed (read and answered in Pulse; never in .env)
Names only. Channels are email, Pulse and push: no SMS, no webhooks (Jason's correction to the report).

Common CrawlSourceOn · Working live03 §26.2 · 3 states
W3 while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped: it can run. Its columnar reads use only data.commoncrawl.org; only the per-site copies wait. W3 does nothing while its two switches stay Off by the system (left by a closed trip): Read a source (task source) and Common Crawl (task commoncrawl), crawl_capture_tasks.enabled = 0, written by a trip before decisions/0175 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (c)). Its trip, pf:wf:W3, is closed: Jason's own Check and start again closed it on Nov 21 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)). Nothing switches them on by itself (0175's note of 2026-11-20, "Keep for a person").
More

Fix it: Switch on: Read a source, then Switch on: Common Crawl. Each runs its switch-on check first (02 row 64) and is logged with who. Its way back: Switch off on the same row (02 row 398), logged.

W3 can run while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped: its columnar bulk reads ask only data.commoncrawl.org (crawler.py:1697–1703; worker 2.16.1, :215). Only the per-site page copy waits on the index (cc_home, crawler.py:1672–1680). Since release #247 (live 12:22 UTC Nov 21) the gate checks data.commoncrawl.org first and the index as a second part that holds only that copy (Preflight.php:1110–1113; reachAll, :895–907). Railway runs that worker (2.16.1).

Source: Railway runs crawler 2.16.1: the session manager confirmed it through Railway's API, ~12:3x UTC Nov 21 (the traversence and w0-indexer deploys SUCCESS at 12:22:18 UTC, commit b2ab69e).

Held: only the needs that go through index.commoncrawl.org (the per-site copies). On a backup: the columnar reads, from data.commoncrawl.org.

Recovers when: a person switches on its two tasks (above). #35 and pf:wf:W3 have closed: the same press on Nov 21 got a 200 from index.commoncrawl.org and closed #35 as Recovered (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)); a later 504 would trip #35 again and hold only the per-site copies.

Can W3 run while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped?
Gemini's hand-off note, 2026-11-22
  • The columnar bulk reads ask only data.commoncrawl.org: common_crawl() holds only on that host and reads the URL Index there, "never the index server" (crawler.py:1697–1703; worker 2.16.1, :215).
  • Only the per-site page copy waits on index.commoncrawl.org: cc_home() (crawler.py:1672–1680), called by W3's fallback (:1880) and W2's Re-read websites (:2415).
  • The gate, since release #247 (live 12:22 UTC Nov 21): Common Crawl's line is data.commoncrawl.org first, the index second (Preflight.php:1110–1113); a failing second part is amber, "Only the copy of one site's page waits; the rest works" (reachAll, :895–907), shown "Partly working" (:41–44). Before #247 the line asked only the index, so its 504 tripped W3 whole: the snapshot (3:19 AM MST) shows that.
  • A SlowDown at data.commoncrawl.org (#22) is a rate wait that pauses the bulk reads while its back-off runs (crawler.py:1602–1609, :1701).
Confirmed: Railway runs crawler 2.16.1 (the session manager through Railway's API, ~12:3x UTC Nov 21: the traversence and w0-indexer deploys SUCCESS at 12:22:18 UTC, commit b2ab69e). pf:wf:W3 is closed: Jason's own Check and start again closed it on Nov 21 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)). What stops W3 now: its two switches, Read a source and Common Crawl, Off by the system (left by a closed trip); the fix is Switch on for each, with its check, and Switch off is its way back.

Can W3 run while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped?Yes: its bulk readsGemini's hand-off note, 2026-11-22 The columnar bulk reads ask only…
Can W3 run while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped?
Gemini's hand-off note, 2026-11-22
  • The columnar bulk reads ask only data.commoncrawl.org: common_crawl() holds only on that host and reads the URL Index there, "never the index server" (crawler.py:1697–1703; worker 2.16.1, :215).
  • Only the per-site page copy waits on index.commoncrawl.org: cc_home() (crawler.py:1672–1680), called by W3's fallback (:1880) and W2's Re-read websites (:2415).
  • The gate, since release #247 (live 12:22 UTC Nov 21): Common Crawl's line is data.commoncrawl.org first, the index second (Preflight.php:1110–1113); a failing second part is amber, "Only the copy of one site's page waits; the rest works" (reachAll, :895–907), shown "Partly working" (:41–44). Before #247 the line asked only the index, so its 504 tripped W3 whole: the snapshot (3:19 AM MST) shows that.
  • A SlowDown at data.commoncrawl.org (#22) is a rate wait that pauses the bulk reads while its back-off runs (crawler.py:1602–1609, :1701).
Note
Confirmed: Railway runs crawler 2.16.1 (the session manager through Railway's API, ~12:3x UTC Nov 21: the traversence and w0-indexer deploys SUCCESS at 12:22:18 UTC, commit b2ab69e). pf:wf:W3 is closed: Jason's own Check and start again closed it on Nov 21 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)). What stops W3 now: its two switches, Read a source and Common Crawl, Off by the system (left by a closed trip); the fix is Switch on for each, with its check, and Switch off is its way back.

Workflows

About this view

W0–W14 from the live Automation::WORKFLOWS, each need from Preflight::NEEDS in the map's order, linked to its card; the fallback is the need's own rule. State: the alarms snapshot, Nov 21, 3:19 AM MST. A source with no card yet is greyed and listed under Coverage.

WorkflowIts needs: sources in order, then the fallbackState
W0 Indexer

Paused by the system
W1: its task overture_bulk failed (run #1290)
W1: its task foursquare_bulk failed (run #1288)
Root cause so far

the response path. The worker sent its rows to our load endpoint (/api/crawl/loads.php) and no reply came within its timeout, though the site stored rows from run #1290. Unconfirmed until the endpoint's own timings for 08:15–08:21 and 08:26–08:32 UTC are read (IR-0001; asks.md, visit 1).

Recovers when

/api/crawl/loads.php's check passes (it replies within its timeout), then overture_bulk and foursquare_bulk next do their work (a town loaded, its records sent). Then W1's two trips close as Recovered.

W2 Keeping listings current
Live listings rechecked: websites, who they are, map points, Google.
  • Confirm a business (W1, W2): our copies agreeing → NPI Registry (CMS) → Arizona Corporation Commission → Tavily → Brave Search → confirm · else the person queue
  • Page prose into facts (W1–W3, W10, W11): Google AI Studio (Gemini) → prose · else "waiting to be read"; nothing lost
  • Re-read websites (W2): Railway → Common Crawl · else waits
  • A missing phone or website (W2): our open-data copies → Tavily → Brave Search · else waits
  • Map points (W2): our ZIP and town points → U.S. Census Bureau · else waits
  • Still open? (W2): our copies' open or closed status → Google Places · else waits
Warning
/api/crawl/refresh counted more than it received
Its count (L9)

The count can't be trusted until the step-4 fix. Cause: "received" counts only the lists in the POST (ControlLedger.php:162, listed() :77–86): the other locations found, never the listing being refreshed (entity_id) or its fields (found). The outcomes count that listing too: updated once (CrawlerIngest.php:571, one line per record, ControlLedger.php:47–56), plus each location sent to Review (IntakeStager.php:222). One listing with one other location: received 1, counted 2 (L9). With no library mark, the answer's filled list counts once per field (Refresh.php:180; ControlLedger.php:28, :97). Fix (step 4): count at the boundary, once.

W3 Sources and the place store
The source register: sites we read regularly, and what they name.
  • Page prose into facts (W1–W3, W10, W11): Google AI Studio (Gemini) → prose · else "waiting to be read"; nothing lost
  • Sources read regularly (W3): what our sources said → Railway → Common Crawl · else waits
  • Semantic search (W3): Supabase → Google AI Studio (Gemini) · else search uses keyword search (0164 §5.2)
Off by the system: 2 switches
Its trip closed (Jason's Check and start again, Nov 21); its two task switches stay Off by the system, left by a closed trip.
Now

W3 does nothing while its two switches stay Off by the system (left by a closed trip): Read a source (task source) and Common Crawl (task commoncrawl), crawl_capture_tasks.enabled = 0, written by a trip before decisions/0175 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (c)). Its trip, pf:wf:W3, is closed: Jason's own Check and start again closed it on Nov 21 (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)). Nothing switches them on by itself (0175's note of 2026-11-20, "Keep for a person").

Fix it

Switch on: Read a source, then Switch on: Common Crawl. Each runs its switch-on check first (02 row 64) and is logged with who. Its way back: Switch off on the same row (02 row 398), logged.

Can W3 run?

W3 can run while index.commoncrawl.org is tripped: its columnar bulk reads ask only data.commoncrawl.org (crawler.py:1697–1703; worker 2.16.1, :215). Only the per-site page copy waits on the index (cc_home, crawler.py:1672–1680). Since release #247 (live 12:22 UTC Nov 21) the gate checks data.commoncrawl.org first and the index as a second part that holds only that copy (Preflight.php:1110–1113; reachAll, :895–907). Railway runs that worker (2.16.1).

Its radius (the contract)

Held: only the needs that go through index.commoncrawl.org (the per-site copies). On a backup: the columnar reads, from data.commoncrawl.org.

Recovers when

a person switches on its two tasks (above). #35 and pf:wf:W3 have closed: the same press on Nov 21 got a 200 from index.commoncrawl.org and closed #35 as Recovered (01-lift-reconstruction.md (b)); a later 504 would trip #35 again and hold only the per-site copies.

Where it stands: root cause and recovery
W2: Its count (L9)
The count can't be trusted until the step-4 fix. Cause: "received" counts only the lists in the POST (ControlLedger.php:162, listed() :77–86): the other locations found, never the listing being refreshed (entity_id) or its fields (found). The outcomes count that listing too: updated once (CrawlerIngest.php:571, one line per record, ControlLedger.php:47–56), plus each location sent to Review (IntakeStager.php:222). One listing with one other location: received 1, counted 2 (L9). With no library mark, the answer's filled list counts once per field (Refresh.php:180; ControlLedger.php:28, :97). Fix (step 4): count at the boundary, once.

Where it stands: root cause and recovery
W2: Its count (L9)
The count can't be trusted until the step-4 fix. Cause: "received" counts only the lists in the POST (ControlLedger.php:162, listed() :77–86): the other locations found, never the listing being refreshed (entity_id) or its fields (found). The outcomes count that listing too: updated once (CrawlerIngest.php:571, one line per record, ControlLedger.php:47–56), plus each location sent to Review (IntakeStager.php:222). One listing with one other location: received 1, counted 2 (L9). With no library mark, the answer's filled list counts once per field (Refresh.php:180; ControlLedger.php:28, :97). Fix (step 4): count at the boundary, once.
